explain.say: A truss bridge is a frame of straight bars joined into triangles. When a train crosses, its weight goes through the deck to the joints of the truss.

explain.say: From each joint the load travels along the diagonal bars toward the ends. Each bar is only pushed or pulled along its length, never bent, so slim bars can carry heavy loads.

faq.q: How does a truss bridge work?
faq.a: A truss bridge uses a frame of triangles. Loads go to the joints and travel along the bars, each of which is either squeezed or stretched, so the frame is stiff and light.
asks: Why do truss bridges use triangles?

faq.q: Are the diagonal bars in tension or compression?
faq.a: It depends on which way they slope. In a Pratt truss the diagonals slope down toward the middle and are stretched, while in a Howe truss they slope the other way and are squeezed.
asks: What do the diagonals do in a truss?

faq.q: What are the top and bottom chords?
faq.a: The chords are the long bars along the top and bottom of a truss. Under load the top chord is squeezed and the bottom chord stretched, just like the top and bottom of a bending beam.
asks: What is a chord in a truss?
Which part of a truss is in tension?

faq.a: A Warren truss uses a row of triangles with diagonals sloping alternately one way then the other, usually with no vertical bars. It is simple and uses little material, so it is common on footbridges and railway bridges.
asks: What does a Warren truss look like?

faq.a: A truss is like a solid beam with most of the middle cut away. The material left is in the chords and diagonals, exactly where the forces flow, so little is wasted.
asks: Why do truss bridges have gaps?
Why use a truss instead of a solid beam?

facts: In a Pratt truss under normal load, the diagonals are in tension and the verticals in compression.
The Pratt truss was patented in 1844 by Thomas and Caleb Pratt.

quiz.say: In a simple truss bridge carrying a heavy train, what is happening to the bottom chord?
quiz.show: The bottom chord of a loaded truss is…
quiz.why: The truss bends like a deep beam, so its bottom edge is stretched while the top chord is squeezed.

wrong.1: That is what happens to the top chord.
wrong.2: Truss bars are joined at their ends, so they carry push or pull along their length rather than bending.
